title: Artin tensor theorem for henselian components, with residue-field dichotomy
statement: For a commutative ring $C$ and a connected component $Z$ of $\operatorname{Spec}C$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], its component ring is $C_Z=C/I_Z$, where $I_Z$ is generated by the idempotents $e\in C$ with $Z\subseteq V(e)$; the canonical closed subscheme $\operatorname{Spec}C_Z$ has underlying space $Z$. Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $B_1,B_2$ ind-etale $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Suppose every component ring of each $B_j$ is henselian local [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Set $B=B_1\otimes_R B_2$. Every component ring of $B$ is henselian local. For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\subset B$, either $B/\mathfrak m$ is separably closed, or there are $j\in\{1,2\}$ and a maximal ideal $\mathfrak n\subset B_j$ with $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m\cap B_j$ such that the induced extension $B_j/\mathfrak n\to B/\mathfrak m$ is separable algebraic.

source.place: Hübner–Schmidt, The tame site of a scheme, §6, component-ring convention on printed p. 12, and Theorem 6.4, printed p. 13, specialized to two factors. No Noetherian, normality, or strict-henselian hypothesis is imposed in Theorem 6.4.
